newsitem.title: USA: House ethics panel votes to punish Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: House ethics panel votes to punish Gingrich.

text.p: The House of Representatives ethics committee on Friday voted 7-1 to recommend that the full House reprimand Speaker Newt Gingrich and levy a $300,000 penalty to help pay for a two-year inquiry into his admitted ethics breaches.

If the House approves the penalty, Gingrich would be the first sitting speaker to be reprimanded formally. The speaker is the third-highest elected official of the United States after the president and vice president.

A reprimand, imposed by the House seven times in the past, is exceeded in severity only by expulsion and censure. An investigative subcommittee concluded Gingrich's offences "fell somewhere in between" reprimand and censure.
Reprimand would allow Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, to remain as speaker, but censure could have forced him out.
